entries.title: Asking again reopens the chat you already started
entries.body: Asking about a glossary term, cited work, idea or Sources claim reopens your existing chat about it rather than starting a second. Its row in the panel shows a mark with a one-line summary of it. The Ask buttons are icons with a card explaining them; on a touchscreen, the first tap shows the card and the second uses it.

entries.title: Empty Reception results say what happened
entries.body: When Reception finds nothing for an article you added, it says which happened: no pages came back; pages came back but the AI picked none out; or the ones it picked could not be confirmed. Where pages did come back, it gives the counts. The Claims description says you choose the article's own claims to check against the web.

entries.title: Skim has a Previous stop button
entries.body: While you walk a Skim route, a ‹ Previous stop button appears on the left from the second stop of each pass, so you can step back without the keyboard. It works on routes you already have, and the left-arrow key still does the same.

entries.title: Cited by works for papers from arXiv
entries.body: Papers added from arXiv always reported having no DOI, the permanent identifier many papers carry, so Cited by never ran for them. They keep the DOI from arXiv's record when the title and authors match, and older imports find theirs from the arXiv address. The note shown when an article has no DOI says what one is.

entries.title: Deeper Skim passes are never shorter
entries.body: A Skim route could give a deeper pass fewer stops than the one before it, so going further showed you less. New and regenerated routes are checked for this, and repaired or rejected before you see them. Routes made earlier stay as they were until you regenerate them.
